title: Resort Digital Marketing Plan: Channels and Order for India
excerpt: A channel-by-channel resort marketing plan for Indian properties, from Google listings and OTAs to your booking engine, search, social and repeat guests, and the order to build them in.
description: A resort digital marketing plan for India: Google listings, OTAs, booking engine, search, social, reviews and WhatsApp, and the order to build them.
html:
A resort digital marketing plan in India works best when channels are added in order: fix your Google Business Profile and Google Hotel listing first, then OTA listings, then a fast website with a booking engine, then search and paid ads, then social, then email and WhatsApp follow-up. Reviews run through every stage.

Why the order matters more than the channel list

Most resort owners already know the channel names. The problem is usually sequence. A property in Coorg that starts running Instagram ads before its Google listing shows correct photos, rates and a working phone number is paying to send people to a weak first impression. Each channel in this plan depends on the one before it. Search ads send people to your website, so the website has to convert. Social posts send people to your Google listing or WhatsApp, so those have to answer questions quickly.

Think of the plan as three layers:

  • Foundation: Google Business Profile, Google Hotel listing and free booking links, OTA listings, and your own website with a booking engine.
  • Demand: search (organic and paid), metasearch and social media.
  • Retention: reviews, email and WhatsApp, and repeat-guest offers.

Get the foundation right before spending on demand. Retention costs the least and is the most often skipped.

Foundation 1: Google Business Profile and Google Hotel listings

When someone searches your resort's name, or "resort near Kabini", Google shows a business panel with photos, reviews, location and, for hotels, a rates and booking section. This is often the first thing a guest sees, before your website or any OTA page.

Check the basics: the correct category (resort hotel, hotel, or similar), accurate address and map pin, phone and WhatsApp numbers that are answered, check-in and check-out times, amenities, and at least a few recent photos of every room type. Answer the questions people post on the listing.

Google also offers free booking links, which let hotels show their own website rate beside OTA rates in that panel, usually through a connection with your booking engine or channel manager. Paid Hotel Ads work in the same space. Ask your booking engine provider whether they support these connections, and check Google's own help pages for current requirements rather than relying on hearsay.

Foundation 2: OTAs as a distribution channel, not the whole plan

MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Booking.com, Agoda and Airbnb reach guests you would not otherwise find. For a new or small resort, they may be most of your bookings in the first year, and that is fine. The cost is commission, so treat it as an acquisition cost per booking, the same way you would treat ad spend.

What to get right on every OTA listing:

  • The same room names, photos and inclusions you use on your own site.
  • A clear cancellation policy and child policy.
  • Prompt replies to guest messages and reviews.
  • Rate and availability synced through a channel manager to avoid overbookings.

The longer-term goal is a healthier mix, where repeat and returning guests book with you directly. The tactics for that are in our guide to increasing direct bookings for a resort.

Foundation 3: Your website and booking engine

Your website is the only channel you fully control. It needs to answer the questions guests actually have: how the room types differ, what meals are included, how to get there from the nearest airport or railway station, whether kids and pets are allowed, and what the cancellation policy is. Then it needs a booking engine that shows the final price with taxes, accepts UPI and cards, and works on a phone.

If you only fix three things on the site, fix these: page speed on mobile, a visible "Check availability" button on every page, and a WhatsApp button that someone actually answers within minutes during the day. For depth, see the posts on resort website UX and booking engine conversion.

Demand: search, metasearch and social

Organic search

Guests search for places and occasions, not brand names: "resort in Wayanad with pool villa", "weekend getaway from Bengaluru", "corporate offsite near Pune". A page on your site for each real offer and each nearby attraction gives you a chance to appear for those searches. This is slower than ads but compounds over time. See SEO and organic growth for how we think about it.

Paid search and metasearch

Google Ads on your own brand name protects searches you have already earned from OTAs bidding on them. Campaigns on non-brand phrases, such as "Udaipur lake view resort", cost more and need a matching landing page. Metasearch (Google Hotel Ads, Trivago and similar) puts your direct rate beside OTA rates. Start small, track cost per booking, and only scale what pays back.

Social media

Instagram and Reels are where many travellers form the "I want to go there" feeling. Social works best as a source of enquiries on WhatsApp and visits to your listing, not as a numbers game for followers. A content plan for this is in the post on resort Instagram and Reels.

Retention: reviews, email and WhatsApp

Reviews on Google, TripAdvisor and the OTAs influence nearly every channel above, because they appear on your listing, in OTA ranking and in guests' decisions. Ask every guest for a review, reply to all of them, and use recurring complaints to fix operations. The detail is in our resort reputation management guide.

Email and WhatsApp are how a one-time OTA guest becomes a direct repeat guest. With permission, keep a simple list of past guests and send a handful of useful messages a year: long-weekend availability, a monsoon package, an anniversary offer. Keep messages short, relevant and easy to opt out of.

A sequencing checklist for the first six months

MonthFocusDone when
1Google Business Profile, OTA listing clean-up, review requestsListings match, photos current, every guest asked for a review
2Website fixes and booking engine checkMobile booking works end to end with UPI, taxes shown upfront
3Google free booking links or metasearch connection; brand-name search adsYour direct rate shows on Google beside OTA rates
4Offer pages for your main packages; tracking in GA4Each offer has its own page and enquiries are counted
5Instagram content plan and WhatsApp enquiry handlingWeekly posting rhythm, replies within an agreed time
6Past-guest email and WhatsApp list; review of channel costsYou know cost per booking by channel

Measuring all of this does not need complex tools. A monthly sheet of bookings, revenue and cost by channel is enough to start; the post on hotel marketing data includes a template. More on our approach for stays is on the hospitality page.

Frequently asked questions

What should a resort do first in digital marketing?

Start with what guests see before they reach you: your Google Business Profile, your OTA listings and reviews. Make photos, room names, policies and contact numbers consistent and current. Then make sure your own website can take a booking on a phone. Only after that does spending on ads or social media make sense, because those channels send people to these places.

Should a small resort stop using OTAs to save commission?

Usually not. OTAs bring guests who would not find you otherwise, and for many small properties they fill rooms that would stay empty. Treat commission as a cost of acquiring a booking and compare it with other channels. The practical goal is a better mix over time, with repeat guests and brand searches booking directly, rather than cutting OTAs off.

How much should a resort spend on digital marketing?

There is no fixed figure that fits every property. Work backwards from cost per booking. Say a stay is worth ₹12,000 and you are willing to spend ₹1,500 to win it; that number sets your ceiling for ads in each channel. Start small with brand-name search and a few offers, measure what each booking costs, and increase spend only where it pays back.

How long does it take to see results?

Listing clean-ups, review replies and booking engine fixes can show up within weeks because they affect guests who are already looking. Brand-name ads work almost immediately. Organic search and social media take longer, often several months, because they depend on building pages, content and trust. Plan for both quick fixes and slower channels at the same time.

Where to start

This week, search your resort's name on Google and on two OTAs from your phone and note every mismatch in photos, room names, policies and phone numbers. Fix those first, then ask every departing guest for a review. Next month, test a full booking on your own website using UPI and list what got in the way.
